question.problem:
$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨(z-{z}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{__________},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(z,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x=z-{z}^{2}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis for $z\in [0,1].$ What is the second component of $r?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14275690/assets/d3302b5f4ea4c0387d70ac8f78e03e486fff9579f1a6b5e5cec08a31cde76af3.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $x=f(z)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $x=f(z)=z-{z}^{2}\ge 0$ for all $z\in [0,1].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨(z-{z}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,(z-{z}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [0,1],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Therefore, the second component of $r$ is $(z-{z}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
